title: I Used the Jewelry-Torch Station Log on the Mentor Who Left My Tips

parts.text: I stepped into torch two at 4:06 p.m. and mentor Sia was already using my numbered tips. The board said: FORTY MINUTES. TIPS STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-seven, bench steward, holding a clipboard that listed our solder. Sia shrugged. "Mentors keep the flame." I photographed the board, the booking, and her flame on my tips. Then I asked for the station log. At 4:14 the bench desk pinged why Sia's flame sat on our tips. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bench desk can see Sia's flame on torch two during our solder.

social.video_title: She left her flame on my numbered tips — Part 1/2
social.description: Jewelry studio, a mentor on my tips, a forty-minute clock she posted. I logged the flame. Would you have asked for the station log?

parts.text: Sia called it pickle tests until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the torch still. The tips went back to my numbered block. Sia ran a slot of their own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS DO NOT KEEP THE FLAME. I keep our solder on a labeled card. Sia brown-bags her flames. The torch finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Station log, numbered tips, and a second line on the board. Were pickle tests ever our solder?
